statement: A running model, not a calibrated one. Its sizes, flowering months and the shape of its year rest on published descriptions of this cultivar and of Clematis viticella (RHS, Bean, Clematis on the Web, the International Clematis Society, Darwin); every rate, count and date between those is an assumption chosen so that the plant reaches what the descriptions say, and none has been measured on a plant. The engine does not branch a shoot in the season it is made, so the flowering side branches of a real stem are stood in for by more stems from the base and by drawing each flowering node as a cyme of three. Use its output to compare scenarios and to show what a design implies, not to predict dates, sizes or loads.

names.basis: Flowers stand clear of the leaves on long stalks from the leaf axils and face outwards, half nodding (HelpMeFind: 'semi-nodding'; Bean: 'opening flat'; RBG Victoria for C. viticella: 'nodding'). The seed heads stay on the same stalks, so they are held the same way. No forms are named: the plant has one kind of leaf, of cyme and of seed head, and the differences between its leaves are drawn as variants.

phenology.budburstDoy.basis: RHS group 3 guide: prune in late winter or early spring 'when buds show signs of growth, typically February'. New shoots are taken to start lengthening on 11 March. No dated record of shoot extension was found.

phenology.growthEndDoy.basis: Shoots are taken to stop lengthening on 29 July, as the plant comes into full flower: a stem is then at the height the descriptions give by the time it flowers. No dated source.

phenology.leafFlushDoy.basis: Leaves open as the shoots that bear them lengthen, from the day after bud break. On a plant cut down each February every leaf is on new growth, so only the first of these dates matters. No dated source.

phenology.autumnColourDoy.basis: No source describes autumn colour for this plant, and none is claimed: the leaves are taken to dull, yellow and brown on the stems between 10 October and 11 November.

phenology.leafFallDoy.basis: Deciduous (RHS); Bean: the summer growth 'dies back in winter'. Leaves are taken to drop between 5 November and 11 December. Dates are not from a source.

phenology.floralInitiationDoy.basis: Flowers on the year's own growth (RHS group 3). Buds are taken to begin forming on 4 May, seven weeks before the first flower can open, and to go on forming on the growth made after that, each node flowering about seven weeks after it is laid down. The date is also what keeps the lower part of each stem in leaf only: see flowering.currentSeasonMinShootM. No dated source.

phenology.flowerOpenDoy.basis: The window in which the first flower of a cyme may open: 21 June to 16 August. In a run the first opens about 1 July, because a node flowers seven weeks after it is laid down and only the upper part of a stem flowers. Read from the published season, not from dated records: RHS 'mid to late summer'; Clematis on the Web July, August, September; Bean 'from July to September' for C. viticella.

phenology.petalFallDoy.basis: Not used while phenology.flowerLastsDays is set: each cyme then lasts its own few weeks. Kept in step with it (13 July to 17 September).

phenology.flowerLastsDays.basis: How long one cyme of three flowers is in flower, from the end flower opening to the last side flower dropping its tepals: each flower is taken to last about two and a half weeks and the side flowers to follow the end one by a week or so. Not timed on a plant. With the opening dates this ends the display by 17 September (Clematis on the Web: July to September).

extension.leaderMPerSeason.basis: Derived, not measured: a group 3 clematis is cut to 15-30 cm every February (RHS) and this one stands 2.5 to 4 m by flowering (RHS; Clematis on the Web; Bean 8 to 12 ft for C. viticella), so a stem makes about that much in a season.

extension.lateralMPerSeasonByOrder.basis: Only an unpruned plant has side branches that last from year to year. Scaled down from the leader rate. Not measured.

extension.whipMPerSeason.basis: Not used while organs.whipShareOfNodes is nothing. Present because every model carries every parameter.

extension.establishmentFactorByYear.basis: RHS: two to five years to ultimate height. Taken as six tenths of full growth in the planting year and nine tenths in the next. Not measured.

architecture.trunkStemStartYears.basis: Two stems in the planting year and a third from below ground in the second. RHS: plant with the crown 5-8 cm deep 'to encourage shoots from below ground'; cut back hard in the first spring 'to encourage multiple stems'. The numbers are chosen, not counted.

architecture.nurseryCaneM.basis: RHS: newly planted clematis are cut back to 15-30 cm above the ground. The plant is taken to go in at the top of that.

architecture.maxBranchOrder.basis: Only an unpruned plant keeps branches long enough to branch again; two orders of them are allowed. A placeholder.

architecture.leaderLengthM.basis: Stem length from the ground at which a stem stops. Set from the published heights (RHS and Clematis on the Web 2.5 to 4 m; Bean 8 to 12 ft for C. viticella; International Clematis Society 10 to 15 ft), a little above the lower figure because a stem tied along a lattice runs farther than it climbs. A height is not a route length, so this is an assumption.

architecture.lateralLengthMByOrder.basis: Only on an unpruned plant. Scaled down from the leader. Not measured.

architecture.lateralLengthSpread.basis: Side branches of an unpruned plant vary by three tenths either way about their length. Chosen so that they are not all alike; not measured.

architecture.lateralChanceByParentOrder.basis: Only on an unpruned plant: the chance that a stem passing a joint of the lattice leaves a bud there that breaks in a later spring. A placeholder.

architecture.budExtraDormancyChance.basis: Only on an unpruned plant: three buds in ten wait a year or two longer before breaking. A placeholder; nothing published on bud dormancy in this plant was found.

architecture.budExtraDormancyYears.basis: Only on an unpruned plant: how much longer such a bud waits. A placeholder.

architecture.maxStemsPerRoute.basis: Clematis stems are slender (Bean) and a gardener ties several along one lath or lets them share a wire; three are allowed before the next looks for another way. RHS: 'guide stems so they spread evenly'. Chosen, not counted.

architecture.maxStemsPerPrimaryMember.basis: A glulam member is wide enough to carry more of these slender stems side by side than a lath is: four. Chosen, not counted.

routing.occupancyCost.basis: How much a shoot is put off a lath or wire by each stem already on it. Set high, so that the stems of a plant fan out over a lattice instead of bunching, as a gardener lays them (RHS: 'guide stems so they spread evenly, which improves flowering and avoids a tangled mass'), and so that the stems from the base start on different members. A tuning value, not a measurement.

routing.downhillCostPerM.basis: A growing shoot is not led downhill. The engine's general value is kept; nothing about this plant bears on it. (A stem that outgrows its support bends over and trails, which the model does not show.)

routing.uphillBonusPerM.basis: How strongly a shoot prefers a rising member. Kept modest, so that a stem led up a lath that is already taken turns along a rail to the next one: with routing.occupancyCost this is what fans the stems out. A tuning value, not a measurement.

routing.straightOnBonus.basis: A shoot tends to carry on along the member it is on. A tuning value, not a measurement.

routing.riserBonus.basis: The first stem, which is set on making height, favours a rising member by this much more. A tuning value, not a measurement.

routing.tierBonus.basis: Almost none: a clematis cut down every year is not laid out in level tiers as a wisteria is. A tuning value.

routing.roleDropChance.basis: A shoot soon forgets which way it was first led and takes whatever way is open. A tuning value.

routing.noise.basis: Chance in the choice of the next member, so that no two stems take the same way for the same reason. The engine's general value; not a measurement.

routing.giveUpCost.basis: Beyond this cost a shoot stops where it is. The engine's general value; not a measurement.

attachment.maxGraspDiameterMm.basis: No measurement exists. The plant holds on with its leaf stalks and the stalks of its leaflets (Darwin 1875; Bean: they 'curl round any slender support'), which are a few centimetres long: one turn round an 8 mm rod takes 25 mm of stalk. So a cable qualifies, timber of any size here does not, and the plant has to be tied to it.

attachment.minPitchM.basis: Not used: the stems of this plant do not twine (Darwin: 'the power of spirally twining is completely lost'). Present because every model carries every parameter.

attachment.pitchPerCircumference.basis: Not used: the stems of this plant do not twine. Present because every model carries every parameter.

organs.leafSpacingM.basis: Stem between one pair of leaves and the next on a long shoot of the year. No measurement was found; set at about the length of a leaf (10 to 13 cm, Bean) and a little under, which is how such a shoot reads in leaf.

organs.leafLengthM.basis: The whole leaf, stalk and all. Bean gives 4 or 5 in for C. viticella (Flora Europaea 10-13 cm); no figure was found for this cultivar, which is a hybrid of it, and it is taken as the same.

organs.leavesPerNode.basis: Bean, of the genus: 'The leaves are always in pairs at each joint'.

organs.spurChance.basis: No spurs: this plant flowers on the growth of the year (RHS group 3), and its old stems carry no short flowering wood.

organs.spurLengthM.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

organs.spurLeafCount.basis: No spurs are modelled for this plant.

organs.racemeLengthM.basis: What one flowering node carries is drawn as one cyme of three flowers (Flora Europaea: flowers solitary or up to three in the leaf axils; Bean: 'solitary ... or several on a branched stalk'), and this is its length from the leaf axil to the face of its end flower. A flower is half as wide as that: 6.5 to 9.5 cm, inside the 5-10 cm of Clematis on the Web (RHS to 10 cm; Bean about 4 in). Bean gives flower stalks of 2 to 4 in for C. viticella; no stalk length was found for the cultivar, so the length itself is an assumption.

organs.whipShareOfNodes.basis: None. Bean, of C. viticella: the summer growth 'dies back in winter nearly to the older stem'. The engine's long free shoots never die back, so on an unpruned plant they would stand as bare stems for good; its new growth is given instead as shoots that last one season (sideShoots). On a plant cut down each February there is no old wood to throw them.

organs.whipsPerYearMax.basis: Not used while organs.whipShareOfNodes is nothing. Present because every model carries every parameter.

organs.whipLengthM.basis: Not used while organs.whipShareOfNodes is nothing. Present because every model carries every parameter.

organs.leafLifespanYears.basis: RHS: foliage deciduous. A leaf lasts the one season.

organs.clearStemHeightM.basis: RHS group 3 guide: left unpruned these clematis go on from where they ended the year before, 'with a bare base'. Old stems are taken to throw no new shoots below a metre. It has no effect on a plant cut down each February, whose stubs are shorter than this.

flowering.competenceYears.basis: Flowers on the year's growth (RHS group 3) and is taken to do so from the first summer, on whatever of its stems grows long enough.

flowering.maturityRamp.basis: Half strength in the planting year, eight tenths in the next, full from the third (RHS: two to five years to full size). A placeholder.

flowering.spurFloralChance.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.unprunedFactor.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.currentSeasonFlowersPerM.basis: Cymes per metre of the flowering part of a stem: nineteen nodes in twenty there carry one. Set to make the display the descriptions give ('masses' of flowers, Clematis on the Web; the flowers hiding most of the foliage, International Clematis Society). Not counted on a plant.

flowering.currentSeasonMinShootM.basis: International Clematis Society: it flowers 'mostly on the upper half of the new wood'. Used to keep the lower part of each stem in leaf only: flower buds first form on 4 May, before any shoot of the year is this long, so only the nodes laid down beyond this length can flower. The length is chosen, not measured.

pruning.summerLeavesKept.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

pruning.winterBudsKept.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

regrowth.shootsPerCut.basis: RHS: cut every stem back 'to the lowest pair of healthy buds, 15-30cm above soil level', and plant deep 'to encourage shoots from below ground'. A stub is taken to give the two shoots of its top pair of buds and two to five more from lower buds and from below ground beside it. The number also stands in for the side branches a real stem throws in its upper half, which the engine cannot make in the season a stem is made. Chosen so that an established plant clothes the lattice across the RHS spread and somewhat beyond when its stems are fanned out; not counted on a plant.

thickening.tipRadiusSquaredMm2.basis: A shoot tip a little over 2 mm thick. Bean: 'stems slender'. No measurement was found.

thickening.radiusSquaredPerMetreMm2.basis: Makes a stem of the year about 4 mm thick at its base by autumn. Slender, wiry stems (Bean). No measurement was found.

thickening.branchShare.basis: How much of a shoot's thickness is added to the stem that bears it: makes the stub of an established plant about 8 mm thick. The engine's general value; not measured on this plant.

fruit.setShare.basis: Half of the cymes are taken to keep at least one head of seed. How often this hybrid sets seed in British gardens was not found in any source.

fruit.lengthM.basis: The seed heads stay on the stalks of the cyme they came from, so the cluster is as long as the cyme was (organs.racemeLengthM). The heads themselves are small: Bean, of C. viticella, 'seed-vessels broad and short' with 'very small tails'.

fruit.swellDays.basis: Days for the head of seed to fill out after the last tepals drop. Not timed on a plant.

fruit.ripenDoy.basis: The heads are taken to brown between 7 September and 27 October. No dated source.

fruit.fallDoy.basis: The seeds have no plumes to hold them (Bean: tails 'devoid of the feathery covering') and are taken to drop as the growth dies back, between 16 November and 21 December. No dated source.

appendages.tendrilNodePattern.basis: Not applicable: clematis have no tendrils. Bean, of the genus: they 'support themselves by means of the leaf-stalks'.

appendages.leafStalkCoilShare.basis: Darwin (1875) found the main leaf stalk and the stalks of the leaflets of C. viticella all sensitive and able to clasp; not every leaf meets the support. Six nodes in ten on a stretch the plant holds by itself are taken to have a stalk wound round it. Not counted.

appendages.leafStalkLengthM.basis: Not the length of the stalk, which no source gives, but the reach of its clasp: from the stem round the far side of the 5 mm cable it holds, with the stalk's own thickness and a little play. The engine puts a clasping stalk where the stem lies against the cable, so this is the length that can be drawn there; the rest of the stalk is the stalk of the leaf at the same node. The same figure as hold.claspReachM in morphology.json. Worked out from the cable, not measured on a plant.

appendages.aerialRootPatchSpacingM.basis: Not applicable: it climbs by its leaf stalks (Bean) and makes no clinging rootlets.

appendages.prickleSpacingM.basis: Taken to be unarmed: no description of this plant read mentions prickles or thorns.

sideShoots.bearingWoodAgeYears.basis: Only an unpruned plant has stems a year old. RHS: left unpruned, growth 'continues from where it ended the previous season'. Last year's stems, and older ones, are taken to break into short leafy flowering shoots each spring.

sideShoots.perMetrePerYear.basis: Only on an unpruned plant: about two nodes in three of its old stems, above the bare base, break in a year (RHS: left unpruned, growth 'continues from where it ended the previous season', and the plant still flowers, 'well above eye level'). A placeholder: not counted.

sideShoots.lengthM.basis: Only on an unpruned plant: the new shoots its old stems throw each spring, leafy and ending in flower. No length was found in any source; set at what such a shoot commonly makes where it has to share the plant's vigour with many others. A real one is lax: it leans out a hand's length, then arches and hangs, or clasps whatever it meets (International Clematis Society: stems that outgrow their supports 'bend and trail' their flowers downwards). The engine draws it standing stiff and free, which is the engine's fault and not a claim about the plant; the length is not shortened to hide it.

sideShoots.lifespanYears.basis: Bean, of C. viticella: the summer growth 'dies back in winter nearly to the older stem'. A shoot of the year is taken to last the one season.

sideShoots.terminalFlowerShare.basis: Only on an unpruned plant: four in five of its short shoots end in a cyme (Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria: flowers 'terminal or axillary'). A placeholder.
